title: Unit Conversion II
summary: Given n types of units indexed from 0 to n-1, conversions are defined by a 2D array where each entry [sourceUniti, targetUniti, conversionFactori] shows that one unit of sourceUniti equals conversionFactori units of targetUniti.
statement: Given n types of units indexed from 0 to n-1, conversions are defined by a 2D array where each entry [sourceUniti, targetUniti, conversionFactori] shows that one unit of sourceUniti equals conversionFactori units of targetUniti. For queries [unitAi, unitBi], calculate the number of unitBi equivalent to one unitAi, expressed as p/q in simplest form, and return p*q^-1 mod 10^9 + 7, where q^-1 is the multiplicative inverse of q modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: The n-1 conversions form one connected unit tree, with either direction usable; factors are invertible modulo 1,000,000,007.
[source,target,factor] means one source unit equals factor target units.
For [A,B], return units B per one A as a modular fraction.
hints: Assign each unit a root-relative value; any A-to-B ratio is then value[B]/value[A].
Traverse the conversion tree bidirectionally, labeling reverse edges with modular inverses.
Propagate root values once, then answer each query with target value times inverse(source value).
Path products are consistent in a tree, and dividing two root paths cancels their shared portion to yield the requested conversion.
editorial: Path products are consistent in a tree, and dividing two root paths cancels their shared portion to yield the requested conversion.

tests.explanation: Relative root values give 6/2=3 and 1/2, whose modular value is 500000004.
Root-relative products and modular division produce [3,12,1,2,83333334].
